someone-glad-to-hear-from-me-tonight.title: Someone glad to hear from me tonight
someone-glad-to-hear-from-me-tonight.line: Even on a night when nobody comes to mind, I can call a line where a person is glad to talk with me for as long as I need.
someone-glad-to-hear-from-me-tonight.writerNotes: Talklines exist now: the Friendship Line for older adults, 988 for anyone in distress, and Seoul's city line. The basic, reachable outcome for the worst evenings.

small-talk-with-strangers-that-lifts-my-.title: Small talk with strangers that lifts my day
small-talk-with-strangers-that-lifts-my-.line: On the bus or in line at the store, I trade a few real sentences with someone new and walk away in a better mood than I expected.
small-talk-with-strangers-that-lifts-my-.writerNotes: Epley's commuter studies: people predict talking to strangers will be worse, and it turns out better. Surprising and doable today.

back-in-touch-with-an-old-friend.title: Back in touch with a friend I'd drifted from
back-in-touch-with-an-old-friend.line: I called a friend I hadn't spoken to in years, and we talked long enough to catch up on what actually matters in our lives.
back-in-touch-with-an-old-friend.writerNotes: The advisory urges picking up calls from friends; Harvard's study ties close ties to lasting happiness. Reconnecting is the fastest route to someone who already knows you.

a-friend-i-talk-with-every-week.title: A close friend I talk with every week
a-friend-i-talk-with-every-week.line: There's at least one person I see or call every week who knows what's going on in my life, and I know what's going on in theirs.
a-friend-i-talk-with-every-week.writerNotes: Hall's numbers (about 200 hours to a close friend) make a weekly habit the realistic path; the dream is the outcome, the weekly friend.

a-weekly-group-that-notices-when-im-miss.title: A weekly group that notices when I'm missing
a-weekly-group-that-notices-when-im-miss.line: Every Saturday I show up to the same free 5k, and the people there ask where I was if I skip a week.
a-weekly-group-that-notices-when-im-miss.writerNotes: parkrun study: friendships formed through repeated attendance. Being missed is the concrete sign of belonging.

a-workshop-where-i-build-things-with-oth.title: A workshop where I build and fix things with others
a-workshop-where-i-build-things-with-oth.line: A couple of mornings a week I work on a project at a shared workshop, and the talk comes easily because our hands are busy.
a-workshop-where-i-build-things-with-oth.writerNotes: Men's Sheds: more than 1,300 in Australia. Side-by-side work suits people who don't like face-to-face small talk.

neighbors-i-eat-dinner-with-every-week.title: Neighbors I eat dinner with a few nights a week
neighbors-i-eat-dinner-with-every-week.line: I live in a building where neighbors take turns cooking shared dinners, so I'm never more than a day or two from a real conversation.
neighbors-i-eat-dinner-with-every-week.writerNotes: Capitol Hill Urban Cohousing: 21 residents, shared dinners three or four nights a week (rechecked on the KUOW page). Needs others to build it, so together.

living-alongside-people-of-a-different-a.title: Living alongside neighbors of a very different age
living-alongside-people-of-a-different-a.line: I share a home with people decades older or younger than me, and we drop in on each other without needing a reason.
living-alongside-people-of-a-different-a.writerNotes: Humanitas in Deventer housed students rent-free among residents mostly over 80. Culture lens: changes who we expect to live with.

a-town-where-eating-with-strangers-is-no.title: A town where sharing meals with strangers is normal
a-town-where-eating-with-strangers-is-no.line: A couple of times a year my whole town sets out tables for shared meals, and I sit down with neighbors I'd never met.
a-town-where-eating-with-strangers-is-no.writerNotes: Denmark Eats Together (weeks 17 and 45) and the Big Lunch each June show a whole country can make shared meals ordinary.

a-checkout-where-nobody-rushes-me.title: A checkout line where the cashier has time to chat
a-checkout-where-nobody-rushes-me.line: At my supermarket there's a lane where the cashier is glad to talk, so I don't feel like I'm holding anyone up.
a-checkout-where-nobody-rushes-me.writerNotes: Jumbo's chat checkouts, part of a Dutch health ministry program. Needs a business to change, so together.

someone-checking-on-my-parent-every-week.title: A familiar visitor checking on my parent every week
someone-checking-on-my-parent-every-week.line: Someone my mom knows stops by her place every week, and I hear how she's doing even though I live far away.
someone-checking-on-my-parent-every-week.writerNotes: La Poste's mail carrier visits, plus the Friendship Line's regular check-in calls. For people whose loneliness worry is a parent's, or who are the parent.

a-dinner-with-new-people-on-my-calendar.title: A dinner with new people already on my calendar
a-dinner-with-new-people-on-my-calendar.line: This week I have a dinner booked with a small group of people I haven't met, matched to me, and I'm looking forward to it.
a-dinner-with-new-people-on-my-calendar.writerNotes: Timeleft books a table of six strangers; Bumble For Friends matches by interests. Booking is a tonight action; the dinner is days away.

a-doctor-who-can-refer-me-to-groups.title: A doctor who refers me to local groups, not pills
a-doctor-who-can-refer-me-to-groups.line: When I tell my doctor I'm lonely, she connects me with someone who finds me a gardening club or a music group nearby.
a-doctor-who-can-refer-me-to-groups.writerNotes: England's social prescribing, with more than 3,300 link workers. Friendship Bench shows lay listeners and peer groups through care systems. A policy change for most places.

a-city-that-answers-when-i-call-about-lo.title: A city that answers when I call about loneliness
a-city-that-answers-when-i-call-about-lo.line: My city runs a loneliness line I can call at any hour, and a local council of support groups follows up so I don't fall through the cracks.
a-city-that-answers-when-i-call-about-lo.writerNotes: Seoul's 120 line beat its yearly goal in six weeks; Japan's 2023 Act asks local governments to set up councils on loneliness.

a-bench-where-saying-hello-is-expected.title: A park bench where saying hello is expected
a-bench-where-saying-hello-is-expected.line: There's a bench near me with a sign saying it's fine to sit and chat, so I can start a conversation without feeling strange.
a-bench-where-saying-hello-is-expected.writerNotes: Avon and Somerset Police chat benches. A small public change that gives people permission to talk.

overlaps.reason: Both are a regular group where you get to know people over repeated weeks; the workshop could read as one example of the weekly group.
Both are about sharing a home with neighbors you see often, and both cite the Seattle cohousing building.
Reconnecting with an old friend can be the start of having a close friend you talk with every week.
Both make shared meals the way people meet; one in a building every week, the other across a town a few times a year.
Both are a line you can call when lonely; the city one adds a local council that follows up.
